title: Pre-Analysis — Flap Carriage Bulletin Cancellation and Re-Issue
abstract: Closed re-analysis of the flap carriage standard, run after four aircraft were found with a flap asymmetry outside the acceptance band, covering the incorrect rigging values and the repair scheme that depends on the roller standard.

sections.objective: Establish how rigging values taken from the inboard carriage reached a bulletin written for the outboard position, decide what the four affected aircraft need, and check what else depends on which roller set is fitted.
sections.findings_summary: Two items were confirmed and the work was delegated for the re-issue. The rigging error itself was traced to a single transcription during kit definition and needed no analysis; the useful work was in what else depends on the roller standard. The repair scheme for the flap track fairing attachment rib carries two crack limits, a longer one for the delivered roller set and a shorter one for the softer surface set, because the load into the rib is higher at the same side play with the softer roller. Nothing in the bulletin told a technician embodying the change that a repair already on the aircraft might move to a shorter limit as a result. That is now stated. The second finding was that the wear measurement task also carries two limit sets and its entry condition did not say which applies after a partial embodiment.
sections.next_steps: Re-issue the bulletin under a new number with the corrected values and a statement about existing repairs. Add an entry condition to the wear measurement task covering a partially embodied aircraft. Delegate the re-issue to customer services engineering.

similarity_seeds: what else on the aircraft depends on which roller set is fitted

tasks.title: Search for content that depends on the roller standard

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin published rigging values taken from the inboard carriage and four aircraft were embodied against them before the error was found. It had to be cancelled rather than revised, because an operator holding the original could otherwise continue to work to it.
expected_findings.resolution: Bulletin cancelled and re-issued under a new number with a before-further-flight action for the four affected aircraft.

expected_findings.rationale: The repair scheme carries a shorter crack limit for aircraft with the softer surface roller, because the load into the rib is higher at the same side play. An aircraft carrying an existing repair moves to the shorter limit at embodiment and nothing in the bulletin said so.
expected_findings.resolution: Statement about existing repairs added to the re-issued bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The wear measurement task carries two limit sets and its entry condition does not say which applies on an aircraft embodied on one side only, which is a real state during a two-visit embodiment.
expected_findings.resolution: Entry condition added for a partially embodied aircraft.

expected_non_findings.reason: The superseding bulletin itself, returned by every search. It is the output of this analysis rather than a finding of it, and listing it as a conflict would confuse the record.

type_data.conclusion: Delegated for re-issue. The dependency of the repair limits on the roller standard was the finding that mattered and had not been stated anywhere.
